name: Data Structures & Algorithms
description: DSA interview preparation covering fundamental data structures, problem-solving patterns, and algorithmic techniques.

children.name: Prefix Sum
children.description: Use cumulative sums to efficiently calculate subarray sums and solve range and exact-sum problems.

children.name: Prefix Sum Fundamentals
children.description: Build cumulative sums and use prefix sums to calculate subarray sums efficiently.

children.name: Prefix Sum with HashMap
children.description: Use prefix sums with a HashMap to solve exact subarray sum problems, including cases containing negative numbers.

children.name: Binary Search
children.description: Use binary search to efficiently search sorted data and monotonic answer spaces.

children.name: Binary Search Fundamentals
children.description: Search for an element in a sorted array using left, right, and middle pointers.

children.name: Binary Search on Answer
children.description: Apply binary search to a monotonic search space when the answer itself is not directly present in the array.

children.name: Heap / Priority Queue
children.description: Heap fundamentals, PriorityQueue operations, Top-K patterns, custom comparators, and advanced heap problems.

children.name: Heap Fundamentals
children.description: Min Heap, Max Heap, peek, add, poll, and heap time complexity.

children.name: Top K Pattern
children.description: Kth Largest, Kth Smallest, keeping K largest or smallest elements using heaps.

children.name: Kth Largest
children.description: Find the Kth largest element using a Min Heap of size K.

children.name: Kth Smallest
children.description: Find the Kth smallest element using a Max Heap of size K.

children.name: Top K Frequent Elements
children.description: Use a frequency HashMap and Min Heap of size K with custom comparator and tie-breaking.

children.name: Custom Heap Comparator
children.description: Design custom PriorityQueue comparators using frequency, distance, and tie-breaking rules to keep the worst candidate at the root.

children.name: K Closest Elements
children.description: Keep K elements with the smallest distance from a target using a Max Heap where the farthest element is the worst candidate.

children.name: K Closest Points
children.description: Use a Max Heap of size K based on x² + y² where the farthest point is the worst candidate and is removed first.

children.name: Merge K Sorted Lists
children.description: Use a Min Heap containing one current element from each sorted list and insert the next element from the list after polling.

children.name: Kth Largest in Stream
children.description: Maintain a Min Heap of size K while processing streaming values.

children.name: Median From Data Stream
children.description: Use two heaps: Max Heap for the smaller half and Min Heap for the larger half while maintaining balanced heap sizes.

children.name: Sliding Window
children.description: Solve contiguous subarray and substring problems by maintaining and efficiently updating a window.

children.name: Fixed Size Sliding Window
children.description: Maintain a window of fixed size and update the result when the window moves.

children.name: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
children.description: Maintain the sum of a fixed-size window by adding the incoming element and removing the outgoing element.

children.name: Maximum Average Subarray
children.description: Find the maximum average of a fixed-size subarray by maintaining the maximum window sum.

children.name: First Negative Number
children.description: Track indexes of negative numbers using a queue to find the first negative number in every fixed-size window.

children.name: Maximum Vowels in Substring
children.description: Maintain the number of vowels in a fixed-size substring by adding the incoming character and removing the outgoing character.

children.name: Variable Size Sliding Window
children.description: Expand and shrink a dynamic window based on a validity condition to find optimal subarrays or substrings.

children.name: Minimum Subarray Length
children.description: Find the minimum-length contiguous subarray whose sum is at least a target using window expansion and contraction.

children.name: Longest Subarray with Constraint
children.description: Find the longest valid subarray by expanding the right pointer and shrinking from the left when the constraint is violated.

children.name: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
children.description: Use a HashSet and sliding window to maintain a substring containing only unique characters.

children.name: At Most K Distinct Characters
children.description: Use a frequency HashMap to find the longest substring containing at most K distinct characters.

children.name: Longest Subarray with At Most K Odd Numbers
children.description: Maintain the count of odd numbers and find the longest contiguous subarray containing at most K odd numbers.

children.name: Longest Subarray with Sum Less Than Target
children.description: For positive integers, maintain a variable window whose sum remains strictly less than the target.

children.name: Sliding Window with Frequency Map
children.description: Use HashMap frequency tracking to maintain character or element counts inside the current window.

children.name: Character Replacement
children.description: Find the longest substring that can be converted into one repeated character using at most K replacements. Required replacements are window size minus maximum frequency.

children.name: Minimum Window with Required Characters
children.description: Find the minimum substring containing all required characters by tracking their frequencies and shrinking a valid window.

children.name: Longest / Shortest Window
children.description: Find the longest or shortest valid contiguous subarray or substring using window expansion and contraction.

children.name: Minimum Length Window
children.description: Once a window becomes valid, repeatedly shrink it to find the smallest possible valid window.

children.name: Maximum Length Window
children.description: Maintain a valid window and update the maximum length whenever the current window satisfies the constraint.

children.name: Counting with Sliding Window
children.description: Count all valid contiguous subarrays by using the current valid window length to determine how many valid subarrays end at the right pointer.

children.name: Count Subarrays with Sum at Most K
children.description: For positive integers, count subarrays with sum less than or equal to K using count += right - left + 1 after restoring window validity.

children.name: Count Subarrays with Product Less Than K
children.description: For positive integers, maintain a product-based sliding window and count valid subarrays using the current window length.

children.name: Sliding Window Pattern Recognition
children.description: Identify when Sliding Window applies and distinguish it from techniques such as Prefix Sum when negative numbers make window behavior unpredictable.

children.name: Two Pointers
children.description: Solve array and string problems using two indices that move based on the problem conditions.

children.name: Opposite Direction Two Pointers
children.description: Start pointers from both ends and move them toward each other based on comparisons or constraints.

children.name: Same Direction Two Pointers
children.description: Use two pointers moving through the array or string at different positions to maintain a valid range.

children.name: Sorted Array Two Pointers
children.description: Use the sorted order to efficiently find pairs or combinations satisfying a target condition.

children.name: Fast and Slow Pointers
children.description: Use pointers moving at different speeds for cycle detection, finding the middle, and related linked-list patterns.

name: System Design
description: Comprehensive study guide covering Low-Level Design (LLD) and High-Level Design (HLD).

children.name: Low-Level Design (LLD) / Object-Oriented Design
children.description: Focuses on classes, objects, interfaces, and design patterns.

children.name: Design Principles (SOLID)
children.description: Core object-oriented design principles to build maintainable, flexible, and scalable software systems.

children.name: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
children.description: A class should have only one reason to change, meaning it should perform only a single job or module responsibility.

children.name: Open/Closed Principle (OCP)
children.description: Software entities should be open for extension, but closed for modification.

children.name: Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
children.description: Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without altering the correctness of the program.

children.name: Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
children.description: Clients should not be forced to depend upon interfaces and methods they do not use.

children.name: Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
children.description: High-level modules should depend on abstractions rather than low-level modules and concrete implementations.

children.name: Design Patterns (Gang of GoF)
children.description: Standard reusable solutions to common software design problems in enterprise systems.

children.name: Creational Patterns
children.description: Mechanisms that deal with object creation mechanisms to increase flexibility and reuse of existing code.

children.name: Singleton Pattern
children.description: Ensure a class has only one instance and provide a global point of access to it.

children.name: Factory Method Pattern
children.description: Define an interface for creating an object, but let subclasses decide which class to instantiate.

children.name: Abstract Factory Pattern
children.description: Provide an interface for creating families of related or dependent objects without specifying concrete classes.

children.name: Builder Pattern
children.description: Separate the construction of a complex object from its representation so that the same construction process can create different representations.

children.name: Prototype Pattern
children.description: Specify the kinds of objects to create using a prototypical instance, and create new objects by copying this prototype.

children.name: Structural Patterns
children.description: Mechanisms that explain how to assemble objects and classes into larger structures while keeping them flexible and efficient.

children.name: Adapter Pattern
children.description: Convert the interface of a class into another interface clients expect, allowing incompatible interfaces to work together.

children.name: Decorator Pattern
children.description: Attach additional responsibilities to an object dynamically to provide a flexible alternative to subclassing.

children.name: Facade Pattern
children.description: Provide a unified interface to a set of interfaces in a subsystem to make the subsystem easier to use.

children.name: Composite Pattern
children.description: Compose objects into tree structures to represent part-whole hierarchies, allowing clients to treat individual objects and compositions uniformly.

children.name: Proxy Pattern
children.description: Provide a surrogate or placeholder for another object to control access to it.

children.name: Behavioral Patterns
children.description: Mechanisms that deal with algorithms and the assignment of responsibilities between objects.

children.name: Observer Pattern
children.description: Define a one-to-many dependency between objects so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified automatically.

children.name: Strategy Pattern
children.description: Define a family of algorithms, encapsulate each one, and make them interchangeable at runtime.

children.name: Command Pattern
children.description: Encapsulate a request as an object, thereby letting you parameterize clients with different requests, queue or log requests, and support undoable operations.

children.name: State Pattern
children.description: Allow an object to alter its behavior when its internal state changes, appearing to change its class.

children.name: High-Level Design (HLD) / System Architecture
children.description: Focuses on system architecture, databases, scaling, and network protocols.

children.name: Architectural Patterns
children.description: High-level architectural patterns for modern distributed and scalable systems.

children.name: Microservices Architecture
children.description: Decomposing applications into small, loosely coupled, independently deployable services.

children.name: Event-Driven Architecture
children.description: Asynchronous communication and workflow management driven by event generation and consumption.

children.name: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
children.description: Separating read and write operations to optimize performance, scalability, and security.

children.name: Serverless Architecture
children.description: Executing applications in stateless compute containers managed entirely by cloud providers.

children.name: Caching Systems
children.description: In-memory data stores and caching strategies to improve system read performance and latency.

children.name: In-Memory Data Stores
children.description: Dedicated distributed memory engines designed for ultra-low latency data access.

children.name: Redis
children.description: In-memory key-value data store supporting rich data structures, persistence, and pub/sub.

children.name: Memcached
children.description: High-performance, multithreaded in-memory key-value cache designed for string-based data storage.

children.name: Caching Strategies
children.description: Application and database synchronization access patterns.

children.name: Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading)
children.description: Application reads from cache first; if missing, reads from DB and populates cache.

children.name: Write-Through
children.description: Data is written to the cache and the backing database synchronously.

children.name: Write-Behind (Write-Back)
children.description: Data is written to the cache immediately and asynchronously batched to the database.

children.name: Refresh-Ahead
children.description: Cache automatically refreshes hot entries before they expire.

children.name: Cache Eviction & Invalidation
children.description: Algorithms and rules for managing capacity limits and data freshness.

children.name: LRU (Least Recently Used)
children.description: Evicts the items that have not been accessed for the longest period of time.

children.name: LFU (Least Frequently Used)
children.description: Evicts the items that have the lowest access frequency.

children.name: TTL (Time-To-Live)
children.description: Automatically invalidates and purges keys after a designated duration.

children.name: Cache Invalidation & Thundering Herd
children.description: Mitigating stale data, cache breakdown, penetration, and thundering herd stampedes.

children.name: Data Management & Storage
children.description: Database paradigms, scaling techniques, and transaction consistency models.

children.name: Database Paradigms
children.description: Structural models and data organization across storage types.

children.name: Relational Databases (RDBMS)
children.description: Structured tables, foreign keys, schema constraints, and normalized models.

children.name: NoSQL Document Stores
children.description: Flexible semi-structured JSON/BSON storage systems like MongoDB.

children.name: NoSQL Key-Value & Column Stores
children.description: High-throughput horizontally partitioned storage such as DynamoDB and Cassandra.

children.name: Database Scaling Techniques
children.description: Approaches for scaling database reads, writes, and capacity across nodes.

children.name: Database Sharding
children.description: Horizontal partitioning of database rows across multiple autonomous machines.

children.name: Read Replicas & Replication
children.description: Distributing read traffic using asynchronous or synchronous primary-replica copies.

children.name: Partitioning Strategies
children.description: Range-based, hash-based, and list-based table partitioning.

children.name: Consistency & Transactions
children.description: Correctness guarantees in single-node and distributed systems.

children.name: ACID Properties & Isolation Levels
children.description: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation (Read Uncommitted to Serializable), and Durability.

children.name: CAP & PACELC Theorems
children.description: Fundamental trade-offs between Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance, and Latency.

children.name: Distributed Transactions (2PC & Saga)
children.description: Managing cross-service transactions using Two-Phase Commit or choreographed/orchestrated Sagas.

children.name: Asynchronous Communication
children.description: Decoupled messaging systems, brokers, and event pipelines.

children.name: Message Brokers & Queues
children.description: Point-to-point and worker queue mechanisms for decoupled processing.

children.name: RabbitMQ
children.description: AMQP-based broker emphasizing routing flexibility, exchanges, and guaranteed delivery.

children.name: Apache Kafka
children.description: High-throughput append-only distributed commit log and event streaming platform.

children.name: Messaging Paradigms & Semantics
children.description: Delivery guarantees and consumption models.

children.name: Publish-Subscribe (Pub/Sub)
children.description: Broadcasting messages to multiple independent consumer subscriptions.

children.name: Delivery Semantics
children.description: Trade-offs and implementations of At-Most-Once, At-Least-Once, and Exactly-Once processing.

children.name: Event Streaming & Consumer Groups
children.description: Partitioned ordered reads and horizontal consumer scale-out in stream processing.

children.name: Security & Identity
children.description: Protocols and standards for system security, user identity, and data protection.

children.name: Authentication & Authorization
children.description: Verifying user identity and enforcing granular permission boundaries.

children.name: OAuth 2.0 & OpenID Connect (OIDC)
children.description: Delegated authorization flows, identity verification, and scopes.

children.name: JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
children.description: Stateless claims-based tokens with cryptographic signing and verification.

children.name: Role-Based & Attribute-Based Access Control (RBAC/ABAC)
children.description: Access policy enforcement models based on roles, groups, and contextual attributes.

children.name: Data Protection & API Defense
children.description: Safeguarding communication channels, endpoints, and stored information.

children.name: Encryption (At-Rest & In-Transit)
children.description: Securing data over the wire with TLS/mTLS and on disk using AES encryption.

children.name: API Security & Rate Limiting
children.description: Throttling, Token Bucket algorithms, CORS, CSRF, and WAF protection.

children.name: Monitoring & Observability
children.description: Tools and practices to track, diagnose, and maintain distributed system health.

children.name: Metrics & Dashboards
children.description: Time-series measurement of system counters, gauges, latencies, and saturation.

children.name: Prometheus
children.description: Pull-based time-series database and alerting engine using PromQL.

children.name: Grafana
children.description: Visualization platform to build interactive operational and business dashboards.

children.name: Distributed Tracing
children.description: End-to-end request propagation across asynchronous distributed services.

children.name: OpenTelemetry & Jaeger
children.description: Vendor-agnostic instrumentation APIs, spans, trace context propagation, and Jaeger UI.

children.name: Centralized Logging
children.description: Aggregation, indexing, and search of structured log output across clusters.

children.name: ELK / OpenSearch Stack
children.description: Logstash/Fluentd collection, Elasticsearch indexing, and Kibana log exploration.

name: SQL
description: Comprehensive SQL interview preparation covering SQL fundamentals, joins, aggregation, subqueries, correlated subqueries, window functions, and Common Table Expressions (CTEs).

children.name: SQL Fundamentals
children.description: Core SQL concepts and query-building fundamentals required for working with relational databases.

children.name: SELECT
children.description: Retrieving columns and records from database tables using SELECT queries.

children.name: DISTINCT
children.description: Removing duplicate rows from query results using DISTINCT.

children.name: WHERE
children.description: Filtering rows based on specified conditions.

children.name: ORDER BY
children.description: Sorting query results in ascending or descending order.

children.name: LIMIT
children.description: Restricting the number of rows returned by a query.

children.name: Aliases
children.description: Using aliases for columns and tables to make SQL queries shorter and easier to understand.

children.name: LIKE
children.description: Pattern matching and filtering string values using LIKE.

children.name: IN
children.description: Checking whether a value belongs to a specified set of values.

children.name: BETWEEN
children.description: Filtering values within an inclusive range.

children.name: NULL Handling
children.description: Understanding NULL values and filtering records involving NULL.

children.name: SQL Command Categories
children.description: Classification of SQL commands based on their purpose.

children.name: DDL
children.description: Data Definition Language commands used to define and modify database structures.

children.name: DML
children.description: Data Manipulation Language commands used to insert, update, and delete data.

children.name: DQL
children.description: Data Query Language used to retrieve data from databases.

children.name: DCL
children.description: Data Control Language used to manage database permissions and access.

children.name: TCL
children.description: Transaction Control Language used to manage database transactions.

children.name: SQL Query Execution Order
children.description: Understanding the logical order in which SQL query clauses are processed.

children.name: FROM
children.description: Identifies the source table or tables from which data is retrieved.

children.name: JOIN and ON
children.description: Combines related rows from multiple tables using join conditions.

children.name: WHERE
children.description: Filters individual rows before grouping and aggregation.

children.name: GROUP BY
children.description: Groups rows based on one or more columns for aggregation.

children.name: HAVING
children.description: Filters grouped results after aggregation.

children.name: SELECT
children.description: Determines the columns and expressions returned in the final result.

children.name: DISTINCT
children.description: Removes duplicate rows from the selected result.

children.name: ORDER BY
children.description: Sorts the final query result.

children.name: LIMIT
children.description: Restricts the number of rows returned.

children.name: Joins
children.description: Combining data from multiple tables using relationships between columns.

children.name: INNER JOIN
children.description: Returns rows where matching records exist in both joined tables.

children.name: LEFT JOIN
children.description: Returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table.

children.name: SELF JOIN
children.description: Joining a table with itself, commonly used for employee-manager relationships.

children.name: JOIN Conditions
children.description: Using ON conditions to correctly relate rows between tables.

children.name: Aggregate Functions
children.description: Calculating summary values across groups or sets of rows.

children.name: COUNT
children.description: Counts rows or non-null values.

children.name: AVG
children.description: Calculates the average value of a numeric column.

children.name: MAX
children.description: Finds the maximum value within a set of rows.

children.name: MIN
children.description: Finds the minimum value within a set of rows.

children.name: GROUP BY
children.description: Groups rows so aggregate functions can be applied independently to each group.

children.name: HAVING
children.description: Filters groups based on aggregate conditions.

children.name: Subqueries
children.description: Using one SQL query inside another query to solve multi-step filtering and comparison problems.

children.name: Basic Subqueries
children.description: Using a nested query to provide a value or result set to an outer query.

children.name: Scalar Subqueries
children.description: Using a subquery that returns a single value for comparison in an outer query.

children.name: Correlated Subqueries
children.description: Subqueries that reference a column from the outer query and are evaluated relative to each outer row.

children.name: Highest Salary Per Department
children.description: Finding employees whose salary equals the maximum salary within their own department.

children.name: Lowest Salary Per Department
children.description: Finding employees whose salary equals the minimum salary within their own department.

children.name: Above Department Average
children.description: Finding employees whose salary is greater than the average salary of their own department.

children.name: Second Highest Per Department
children.description: Finding the second-highest distinct salary within each department using correlated subqueries.

children.name: Salary Compared With Manager
children.description: Comparing an employee's salary with the salary of their manager.

children.name: Manager Team Average
children.description: Comparing an employee's salary with the average salary of employees sharing the same manager.

children.name: EXISTS
children.description: Testing whether a correlated subquery returns at least one matching row.

children.name: NOT EXISTS
children.description: Testing whether a correlated subquery returns no matching rows.

children.name: ANY
children.description: Comparing a value against at least one value returned by a subquery.

children.name: ALL
children.description: Comparing a value against every value returned by a subquery.

children.name: Duplicate Detection
children.description: Finding employees with duplicate salaries while excluding the current employee from the comparison.

children.name: Unique Values Within Group
children.description: Finding employees whose salary occurs only once within their department.

children.name: Window Functions
children.description: Performing calculations across related rows while preserving individual rows in the result.

children.name: PARTITION BY
children.description: Divides rows into logical groups for window calculations without collapsing the rows.

children.name: Window ORDER BY
children.description: Defines the ordering of rows inside each window partition.

children.name: ROW_NUMBER
children.description: Assigns a unique sequential number to each row within a window partition.

children.name: RANK
children.description: Assigns the same rank to tied values while leaving gaps after ties.

children.name: DENSE_RANK
children.description: Assigns the same rank to tied values without leaving gaps after ties.

children.name: SUM OVER
children.description: Calculating totals and running totals using SUM as a window function.

children.name: Department Total
children.description: Calculating the total salary for each department while keeping every employee row.

children.name: Running Total
children.description: Calculating cumulative salary values according to a defined row ordering.

children.name: AVG OVER
children.description: Calculating averages across window partitions without collapsing individual rows.

children.name: Department Average
children.description: Adding the department's average salary to every employee row.

children.name: Moving Average
children.description: Calculating an average over a limited number of preceding rows and the current row.

children.name: LAG
children.description: Accessing a value from a previous row within an ordered window.

children.name: Previous Salary
children.description: Retrieving the previous employee's salary within the same department.

children.name: Salary Difference
children.description: Comparing the current employee's salary with the previous employee's salary.

children.name: LEAD
children.description: Accessing a value from the next row within an ordered window.

children.name: Next Salary
children.description: Retrieving the next employee's salary within the same department.

children.name: Window Frames
children.description: Controlling exactly which rows are included in a window calculation.

children.name: UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
children.description: Starts the window frame from the first row of the partition.

children.name: CURRENT ROW
children.description: Defines the current row as the end or starting point of a window frame.

children.name: N PRECEDING
children.description: Includes a specified number of rows before the current row.

children.name: ROWS BETWEEN
children.description: Defines a row-based window frame for calculations such as running totals and moving averages.

children.name: Top N Per Group
children.description: Finding the top employees within each department using ranking window functions.

children.name: Second Highest Per Group
children.description: Finding the second-highest distinct salary per department using DENSE_RANK.

children.name: Window Function With Subquery
children.description: Using a subquery to filter results based on a calculated window-function alias.

children.name: Common Table Expressions (CTE)
children.description: Using named temporary query results to structure complex SQL queries into readable and reusable logical steps.

children.name: CTE Fundamentals
children.description: Understanding the WITH clause and defining a named temporary result set.

children.name: Basic CTE
children.description: Creating a CTE and using it in the main SELECT query.

children.name: CTE With Aggregation
children.description: Using GROUP BY and aggregate functions inside a CTE.

children.name: CTE With HAVING
children.description: Filtering aggregated groups inside a CTE using HAVING.

children.name: CTE With Window Functions
children.description: Combining CTEs with window functions such as DENSE_RANK for multi-step queries.

children.name: Multiple CTEs
children.description: Defining multiple CTEs in a single WITH clause and combining their results.

children.name: CTE With JOIN
children.description: Joining a CTE with the original table or another CTE to solve multi-step problems.

children.name: CTE vs Subquery
children.description: Understanding when a named CTE provides better readability and structure than nested subqueries.

children.name: Interview Problem-Solving Patterns
children.description: Practical SQL patterns repeatedly used in interview questions and real-world query development.

children.name: Highest Salary
children.description: Finding the highest salary globally or within each department.

children.name: Second Highest Salary
children.description: Finding the second-highest salary using subqueries and ranking techniques.

children.name: Highest Salary Per Department
children.description: Finding all employees tied for the highest salary in each department.

children.name: Second Highest Salary Per Department
children.description: Finding employees with the second-highest distinct salary in each department.

children.name: Above Department Average
children.description: Finding employees earning more than their department's average salary.

children.name: Below Department Maximum
children.description: Finding employees whose salary is below the highest salary in their department.

children.name: Duplicate Salary Detection
children.description: Finding employees sharing the same salary within a department.

children.name: Employees With Higher-Paid Coworker
children.description: Finding employees who have at least one coworker earning more in the same department.

children.name: Exactly One Higher-Paid Coworker
children.description: Finding employees with exactly one coworker earning a higher salary.

children.name: Manager Salary Comparison
children.description: Comparing employee salaries with their managers and manager teams.

children.name: Top N Per Department
children.description: Finding a fixed number of highest-paid employees per department using ROW_NUMBER.
